featured_reviews.name: Ashish Balachandran
featured_reviews.review_text:
❌ Urban Tadka – Mulund West: Inconsistent Food, Disappointing Execution

Visited Urban Tadka in Mulund West expecting a rich North Indian dining experience, but sadly, the evening was filled with more misses than hits. The vibe and branding promise a lot—but the food didn’t live up to it.

⸻

🍗 Happy Chicken Tikka – Underdone & Flat

The chicken was quite raw inside, with spices that felt slapped on rather than blended in. Texture was off and flavor didn’t settle. Disappointing, especially for something that’s supposed to be a highlight.

⸻

🐟 Fish Tikka – The Only Redeemer

This was the best dish of the evening. Perfectly cooked, well spiced, flaky and hot. If only the rest of the meal had matched this level.

⸻

🌶️ Garlic Chutney – Always Great

Still one of their strengths—bold, spicy, and garlicky. Goes well with almost anything.

⸻

🫓 Masala Papad – Shockingly Bad

I’ve had good masala papad here in the past, but this time it was very poorly done—soggy in parts, unevenly topped, and clearly rushed. It was a huge letdown, especially for such a simple dish.

⸻

🍷 Sangria – Just Syrupy Sweetness

This wasn’t sangria—it tasted like fruit syrup mixed with soda. No wine flavour, no balance, and way too sweet. It felt like a mocktail trying to pass as something it’s not.

⸻

🍮 Jalebi & Rabadi – Uneven Again
•	Rabadi: Thick, creamy, and well-made. A small win at the end of the meal.
•	Jalebi: Absolutely terrible. Not only was it soggy and bland, but it had a strong chemical smell—almost like bleach, which was shocking and off-putting.

⸻

💬 Final Thoughts

Urban Tadka Mulund is clearly struggling with quality control. From raw chicken and bad jalebi to sloppy basics like masala papad, this meal felt rushed and careless. The fish tikka, garlic chutney, and rabadi were the only saving graces.

⸻

❌ Final Verdict

Not worth the hype or the price. When half the items are badly executed—and one smells like cleaning fluid—it’s a red flag.
Urban Tadka needs to seriously rework their kitchen consistency if they want to live up to their name.

Would not return in a hurry.
🍗👎🍮🥴

featured_reviews.name: Abdul Qawi Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐ Behrouz Biryani – Detailed Review

🍗 Food Quality & Taste

Behrouz Biryani specializes in Mughlai-style biryanis, inspired by “Persian royal recipes.”

Taste: The biryani is rich, aromatic, and slightly on the spicier side with a royal blend of spices and saffron.

Rice Quality: Long-grain basmati rice is used, perfectly cooked — not sticky, and carries the fragrance of ghee and spices.

Meat & Portion: Chicken and mutton pieces are tender and well-marinated. Quantity is sufficient for one hungry person (or two with light appetite).

Vegetarian Options: The Veg and Paneer biryanis are flavorful with saffron aroma, though meat lovers might find them less satisfying.

Popular picks:

Murg Dum Biryani: Juicy chicken, aromatic and perfectly balanced in spices.

Kofta Biryani: Rich and creamy, with mildly spiced meatballs.

Zaikedaar Paneer Biryani: For vegetarians, it’s the most recommended option.

🧆 Sides & Extras

Comes with mint raita and gulab jamun (depending on the combo).

Raita is refreshing and complements the heavy biryani taste.

Gulab jamun is soft and perfectly sweet, a nice royal touch.

📦 Packaging

The packaging is excellent — leakproof, layered, and hygienic.

Each box is sealed and often includes a spoon, tissue, and a little story about “Behrouz – The Lost Kingdom of Biryani.”

Presentation feels premium and suitable for gifting or formal lunch orders.

💰 Price

Slightly higher than local biryanis (₹250–₹450 per portion), but justified by quality and portion size.

Occasional discounts are available on Swiggy, Zomato, and the Behrouz app.

🚚 Delivery

Delivery is usually quick and food arrives hot due to efficient packaging.

Even after 30–40 minutes, rice stays fluffy and non-sticky.

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re anywhere near Paanch Rasta in Mulund West and looking for a place that delivers both exceptional food and genuinely warm hospitality, Sandeep Restaurant & Bar is a spot you should not miss.

In a city like Mumbai, where dining options are endless, what truly sets a restaurant apart is consistency and the way they treat their guests. Sandeep Restaurant excels at both.

Let’s start with the food. Their Prawns Koliwada is an absolute must try. Perfectly marinated, crisp on the outside, juicy inside, and seasoned just right. It carries that authentic coastal flavour without being overly greasy or heavy. The Butter Chicken is rich, balanced and comforting, with a smooth gravy that pairs beautifully with naan or jeera rice. And the Fish Curry deserves a special mention. Fresh, flavourful and well spiced, it feels homely yet restaurant refined at the same time. You can tell that quality ingredients and experience go into every dish.

However, what truly elevates the experience is the hospitality. The entire staff operates with professionalism, attentiveness and warmth that feels rare today. They are quick without being intrusive, polite without being mechanical, and genuinely attentive to every table. There is a sense of discipline and care in the way they coordinate service, which makes dining here smooth and enjoyable.

A special appreciation for the lead staff member, Satish Anna. His presence on the floor reflects leadership and experience. He ensures everything runs seamlessly and makes guests feel personally welcomed. That kind of involvement from senior staff creates a big difference in overall experience.
Sandeep Restaurant is not just about good food. It is about feeling valued as a guest. Whether you are coming with family, friends or colleagues, you can expect consistent quality, generous portions and a team that truly understands hospitality.

Highly recommended for anyone in and around Mulund West looking for a reliable, satisfying and welcoming dining experience

featured_reviews.name: Vinod
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sandeep Bar and Restaurant used to be one of the best places in Mulund — both for food and service. Sadly, it’s not the same anymore. The service has gone from excellent to absolutely terrible. The manager is extremely rude and doesn’t even bother to answer calls. When I tried calling to complain about an incorrect order, he hung up on me mid-conversation — very unprofessional.

The food quality has also gone down noticeably. The ingredients don’t taste as fresh as they once did, and the overall flavor has become quite average.

But the biggest disappointment is the attitude of the staff and management. They clearly don’t care about regular or family customers anymore — it feels like they only want to cater to drunkards.

It’s sad to see such a reputed restaurant lose its charm because of poor management and arrogance. I genuinely hope they improve, but for now, I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone.
